_what: What a JUDGE is shown for nine clause links whose definitions in ontology/kinds.json were written from the gold passages and quote them (2026-10-15: two rounds of stripping examples by pattern still leaked 'Aaron stretched out ... struck' and 'just as the LORD had said'). Each restates the definition's rules in general terms with no example from any verse. The definitions in kinds.json are unchanged; these are only what a calibration judge reads, so the verses it is scored on are not in its instructions.
content: A speech clause and what was said. The said clause is embedded: it is inside the speaking, not next on the narrative line. Where what was said is a run of commands joined by 'and' at one level, the content is that whole collection (the imperative group), not its first command.
within: A clause nested in a role of another clause, as the grammar nests it: for example an infinitive clause that is the object of a verb, or a relative clause inside a noun phrase. The link carries the role it fills.
purpose: What an action is FOR. Two forms. (1) A command, then waw + jussive, cohortative or yiqtol in a DIFFERENT person; it looks forward, where 'because' looks back. A cohortative after a jussive is a promise, not a purpose. (2) A clause nested in a prepositional role as lamed + infinitive construct, saying what an act was done to achieve. NOT where the infinitive completes the main verb (after be able, do again, begin, finish, be willing, refuse, seek, know how, cease, hurry), nor after a verb of speaking or intending, where it is what was said or intended, nor after hayah or natan, nor the quotative le'mor.
result: A command and what it brings about: an imperative, then waw + a third-person weqatal saying what will come of it. The clause-to-clause link; inside the imperative group the same clause is the group's `effect`. Not a plain 'and'.
failed_result: A kind of `result`: the outcome of an attempt, where the outcome is that the attempt's purpose was NOT achieved. Marked by an attempt that has a `purpose`, then 'and' + a negated verb of being able.
fulfils: A report that a command was carried out. (1) Where the text says so with a pro-form: a narrative asah + ken ('did so') or hayah + ken ('it was so'), not negated, with no named subject, after a command. It points at the nearest preceding command (not a cohortative), or at its collection; its implicit 'they' is the ones the command chain was addressed to. (2) THEN, MEMBER BY MEMBER: each narrative clause after such a report that repeats a command's verb fulfils THAT command (and elaborates the report); one that repeats the verb of the command's effect fulfils the effect, and is the `result` of the acts before it.
as: A comparison: ke or ka'asher ('just as') before a clause nested in this one's prepositional role. Where the compared clause is a SAYING ('just as someone had said'), the action is declared the fulfilment of an earlier word.
likewise: Someone else doing the same as a deed just done, where the text says so with ken ('so, thus'): a narrative 'did so' with a NAMED subject that is not doing what it was commanded. Imitation, not fulfilment. Link it only to a deed done after the latest command, so that a named person carrying out a request is not read as copying.
elaborates: A clause giving the detail of an earlier one. Where it is structural: after an asah + ken ('did so') report, the narrative clauses that repeat a fulfilled command's verb are the detail of what was done; each elaborates the report and fulfils its own command.
